[![maintained with tend](https://img.shields.io/badge/maintained_with-tend-bba580?style=for-the-badge&logo=data:image/svg%2bxml;base64,)](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend)

> **November 2026**: Worktrunk was [released](https://x.com/max_sixty/status/2006077845391724739?s=20) at the start of the year, and has quickly become the most popular git worktree manager. It's built with love (there's no slop!). Please let me know any frictions at all; I'm intensely focused on continuing to make Worktrunk excellent, and the biggest help is folks posting problems they perceive.

Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel.

Worktrunk's three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches. Plus, Worktrunk has a bunch of quality-of-life features to simplify working with many parallel changes, including hooks to automate local workflows & copy-on-write build caches.

A quick demo:

![Worktrunk Demo](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/max-sixty/worktrunk-assets@main/assets/docs/light/wt-core.gif)

> ### 📚 Full documentation at [worktrunk.dev](https://worktrunk.dev) 📚

<!-- ⚠️ AUTO-GENERATED from docs/src/content/docs/worktrunk.md#context-git-worktrees..worktrunk-makes-git-worktrees-as-easy-as-branches — edit source to update -->

## Context: git worktrees

AI agents like Claude Code and Codex can handle longer tasks without
supervision, such that it's possible to manage 5-10+ in parallel. Git's native
worktree feature gives each agent its own working directory, so they don't step
on each other's changes.

But the git worktree UX is clunky. Even a task as small as starting a new
worktree requires typing the branch name three times: `git worktree add -b feat
../repo.feat`, then `cd ../repo.feat`.

## Worktrunk makes git worktrees as easy as branches

Worktrees are addressed by branch name; paths are computed from a configurable template. Commands that take a branch also accept the path of the worktree it is checked out in.

<p class="workflow-stage">Start with the core commands</p>

**Core commands:**

<table class="cmd-compare">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Task</th>
      <th>Worktrunk</th>
      <th>Plain git</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Switch worktrees</td>
      <td data-label="Worktrunk"><code>wt switch feat</code></td>
      <td data-label="Plain git"><code>cd ../repo.feat</code></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Create + start Claude</td>
      <td data-label="Worktrunk"><code>wt switch -c -x claude feat</code></td>
      <td data-label="Plain git"><pre><code>git worktree add -b feat ../repo.feat && \
cd ../repo.feat && \
claude</code></pre></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Clean up</td>
      <td data-label="Worktrunk"><code>wt remove</code></td>
      <td data-label="Plain git"><pre><code>cd ../repo && \
git worktree remove ../repo.feat && \
git branch -d feat</code></pre></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>List with status</td>
      <td data-label="Worktrunk"><code>wt list</code></td>
      <td data-label="Plain git"><span class="cmd-compare-value"><code>git worktree list</code> (paths only)</span></td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p class="workflow-stage">Expand into the more advanced commands as needed</p>

<p class="workflow-heading"><strong>Workflow automation:</strong></p>

- **[Hooks](https://worktrunk.dev/hook/)** — run commands on create, pre-merge, post-merge, etc
- **[LLM commit messages](https://worktrunk.dev/llm-commits/)** — generate commit messages from diffs
- **[Merge workflow](https://worktrunk.dev/merge/)** — squash, rebase, merge, clean up in one command
- **[Interactive picker](https://worktrunk.dev/switch/#interactive-picker)** — browse worktrees with streaming CI status and diff, log, PR and comment previews
- **[Share build caches](https://worktrunk.dev/step/#wt-step-copy-ignored)** — ten worktrees get `target/`, `node_modules/`, etc without building or copying them (on APFS, btrfs, and XFS)
- **[`wt list --full`](https://worktrunk.dev/list/#full-mode)** — [CI status](https://worktrunk.dev/list/#ci-status) and [AI-generated summaries](https://worktrunk.dev/list/#llm-summaries) per branch
- **[PR checkout](https://worktrunk.dev/switch/#pull-requests-and-merge-requests)** — `wt switch pr:123` to jump straight to a PR's branch
- **[Dev server per worktree](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/#dev-server-per-worktree)** — `hash_port` template filter gives each worktree a unique port
- **[Aliases](https://worktrunk.dev/extending/#aliases) & [per-branch variables](https://worktrunk.dev/config/#wt-config-state-vars)** — custom `wt <name>` commands and branch-scoped state for hook templates
- ...and **[lots more](#next-steps)**

Multiple parallel agents, same simple commands:

![Worktrunk omnibus demo: multiple Claude agents in Zellij tabs with hooks, LLM commits, and merge workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/max-sixty/worktrunk-assets/main/assets/docs/light/wt-zellij-omnibus.gif)

<!-- END AUTO-GENERATED -->

<!-- ⚠️ AUTO-GENERATED from docs/src/content/docs/worktrunk.md#install..next-steps — edit source to update -->

## Install

**Homebrew (macOS & Linux):**

```bash
brew install worktrunk && wt config shell install
```

Shell integration allows commands to change directories.

**Cargo:**

```bash
cargo install worktrunk && wt config shell install
```

<details>
<summary><strong>Windows & other</strong></summary>

**Windows.** `wt` defaults to Windows Terminal's command, so Winget additionally installs Worktrunk as `git-wt` to avoid the conflict:

```bash
winget install max-sixty.worktrunk
git-wt config shell install
```

Alternatively, disable Windows Terminal's alias (Settings → Apps → Advanced app settings → App execution aliases → "Terminal"/"Terminal Preview") to use `wt` directly.

> Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/) — [policy](https://worktrunk.dev/code-signing/).

**Arch Linux:**

```bash
sudo pacman -S worktrunk && wt config shell install
```

**Conda / Pixi** (community-maintained [feedstock](https://github.com/conda-forge/worktrunk-feedstock)):

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge worktrunk && wt config shell install
```

Or with [Pixi](https://pixi.sh): `pixi global install worktrunk && wt config shell install`.

</details>

## Quick start

Create a worktree for a new feature:

```console
$ wt switch --create feature-auth
✓ Created branch feature-auth from main and worktree @ ~/repo.feature-auth
```

This creates a new branch and worktree, then switches to it. Do your work, then check all worktrees with [`wt list`](https://worktrunk.dev/list/):

```console
$ wt list
  Branch        Status      HEAD±     main↕    main…±    Remote⇅  Commit    Age  Message
@ feature-auth  +   ↑      +27   -8   ↑1       +31                4bc72dc    2h  Add authenticatio…
^ main              ^⇡                                    ⇡1      0e631ad    1d  Initial commit

○ Showing 2 worktrees, 1 with changes, 1 ahead, hidden: Path
```

The `@` marks the current worktree. `+` means staged changes, `↑1` means 1 commit ahead of main, `⇡` means unpushed commits.

When done, either:

**PR workflow** — commit, push, open a PR, merge via GitHub/GitLab, then clean up:

```bash
wt step commit                    # commit staged changes
gh pr create                      # or glab mr create
wt remove                         # after PR is merged
```

**Local merge** — squash, rebase onto main, fast-forward merge, clean up:

```console
$ wt merge main
◎ Generating commit message and committing changes... (2 files, +53, no squashing needed)
  Add authentication module
✓ Committed changes @ a1b2c3d
◎ Merging 1 commit to main @ a1b2c3d (no rebase needed)
  * a1b2c3d Add authentication module
   auth.rs | 51 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
   lib.rs  |  2 ++
   2 files changed, 53 insertions(+)
✓ Merged to main (1 commit, 2 files, +53)
◎ Removing feature-auth worktree & branch in background (same commit as main, _)
○ Switched to worktree for main @ ~/repo
```

For parallel agents, create multiple worktrees and launch an agent in each:

```bash
wt switch -x claude -c feature-a -- 'Add user authentication'
wt switch -x claude -c feature-b -- 'Fix the pagination bug'
wt switch -x claude -c feature-c -- 'Write tests for the API'
```

The `-x` flag runs a command after switching; arguments after `--` are passed to it. Configure [post-start hooks](https://worktrunk.dev/hook/#hook-types) to automate setup (install deps, start dev servers).

## Next steps

- Learn the core commands: [`wt switch`](https://worktrunk.dev/switch/), [`wt list`](https://worktrunk.dev/list/), [`wt merge`](https://worktrunk.dev/merge/), [`wt remove`](https://worktrunk.dev/remove/)
- Set up [hooks](https://worktrunk.dev/hook/) for automated setup
- Explore [LLM commit messages](https://worktrunk.dev/llm-commits/), [interactive
  picker](https://worktrunk.dev/switch/#interactive-picker), [Claude Code integration](https://worktrunk.dev/claude-code/), [CI
  status & PR links](https://worktrunk.dev/list/#ci-status)
- Browse [tips & patterns](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/) for recipes: aliases, dev servers, databases, agent handoffs, and more
- [Extending Worktrunk](https://worktrunk.dev/extending/) — customize workflows with hooks & aliases
- Watch [@DevOpsToolbox's video on Worktrunk](https://youtu.be/WBQiqr6LevQ?t=345)
- Run `wt --help` or `wt <command> --help` for quick CLI reference

<!-- END AUTO-GENERATED -->

vercel-labs/agent-desktop

Computer use CLI for AI agents

Language: Rust

Stars: 15,030

Forks: 1,039

Stars today: 2,470 stars today

README

# agent-desktop

Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

<p>
  <a href="https://vercel.com/labs#labs-products"><img alt="Vercel Labs Product" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/LABS-PRODUCT-0a0a0a.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=Vercel&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-desktop"><img alt="npm version: agent-desktop" src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/agent-desktop.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/blob/main/LICENSE"><img alt="License: Apache-2.0" src="https://img.shields.io/github/license/vercel-labs/agent-desktop.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-desktop"><img alt="npm downloads per month: agent-desktop" src="https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/agent-desktop.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000&label=npm%20downloads" height="28"></a>
</p>

agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library.

Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g agent-desktop
agent-desktop status                # platform, permissions, supported surfaces
agent-desktop permissions --guide   # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant
```

Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64.
For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable.

On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet.
The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket.

Release archives and building from source are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/installation).

## Quick start

```bash
agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i      # interactive elements, each with a ref
agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8            # act on a ref from that snapshot
agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i      # observe again to verify
```

Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot:

```json
{
  "version": "2.6",
  "ok": true,
  "command": "snapshot",
  "data": {
    "app": "Finder",
    "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9",
    "ref_count": 59,
    "complete": true,
    "tree": {
      "role": "window",
      "name": "Downloads",
      "children": [
        { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

- Refs carry their snapshot id. A bare `@e8` fails with `INVALID_ARGS`.
- If the UI changed, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`. Take a new snapshot and use its refs.
- Actions are headless by default: no pointer movement, no focus change. Pass `--headed` for physical input.
- In PowerShell, quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator.

The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/quick-start).

## How it works

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/architecture-dark.png">
  <img alt="The calling agent runs the agent-desktop CLI or the C library. Both go through agent-desktop-core and the PlatformAdapter trait to one platform crate, chosen at compile time, which reads the target app through the AX API on macOS, UI Automation on Windows, or AT-SPI on Linux." src="assets/architecture-light.png" width="720">
</picture>

Your agent calls the CLI, or the C library in process. Both run the same core, which reaches the OS only through `PlatformAdapter`. Each binary is built for one OS and talks to that OS's accessibility API.

## For AI agents

The binary carries guides that match its version:

```bash
agent-desktop skills get desktop      # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules
agent-desktop skills get platform     # what differs on the OS you run on
agent-desktop <command> --help        # flags for one command
```

Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop):

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop
```

Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run
`agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them.
```

Retry a failed command only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. See [JSON output](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/json-output) for the envelope, error codes, and exit codes.

### MCP

`agent-desktop mcp` serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio. A tool is named after its command (`desktop_snapshot`, `desktop_click`, `desktop_session_start`), takes that command's arguments, and returns its JSON envelope:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "agent-desktop": { "command": "agent-desktop", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

Global flags given to `mcp`, such as `--session`, `--headed` or `--trace`, apply to every call.

## Commands

agent-desktop has 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/commands) documents each one.

| Group | Commands |
|---|---|
| Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` |
| Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` |
| Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` |
| Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` |
| Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` |
| Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` |
| Wait | `wait` |
| Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` |
| System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` |

## Platform support

| Platform | Requirement | Accessibility API |
|---|---|---|
| [macOS](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/macos) | macOS 13 or later, Intel or Apple Silicon | AX API |
| [Windows](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/windows) | Windows 10 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64 | UI Automation |
| [Linux](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/linux) | Ubuntu 24.04 or later, x86_64 or aarch64, X11 or Wayland | AT-SPI |

Each platform page lists what works headless, what needs `--headed`, and what refuses.

## C library

Each release ships `libagent_desktop_ffi`, so a program can call agent-desktop in process. See the [C library docs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/ffi).

```python
import ctypes
lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib")
lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
assert lib.ad_init(7) == 0  # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library
adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create()
lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter)
```

## Development

Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS:

```bash
HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi)
cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}"
cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

On Windows, use `agent-desktop-windows` instead of `agent-desktop-macos`; on Linux, `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop): what it is and how it works
- [Snapshots and refs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/snapshots-and-refs)
- [Errors and recovery](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/errors-and-recovery)
- [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/skills)
- [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md): vocabulary
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md)

ZapFast is a WhatsApp client written in Rust with
[egui](https://www.egui.rs) and [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the
framework behind a family of native desktop apps. It links to your phone as a
companion device through
[whatsapp-rust](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust) and has no browser
engine. In our Linux test it opens in under a second and uses about 200 MB of
idle RAM, against 1.13 GB for WhatsApp Web.
[See the measurements](https://zapfast.rocks/benchmarks/).

The interface is available in English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional),
French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Spanish,
and Turkish.

## Your chats, on your desktop

| Feature | What you can do |
|---|---|
| **Messages** | Send formatted text, replies, edits, reactions, forwards, pictures, files, stickers, GIFs, polls, and voice messages. |
| **Media in the chat** | Play voice messages, videos, round video messages, GIFs, and animated stickers in place. |
| **Your history** | Keep your chats in an encrypted archive on this computer, fetch older messages from your phone as you scroll, and export locally saved chat history as text or a ZIP with downloaded attachments. |
| **Several numbers** | Link more than one WhatsApp number and switch between them in one window. |
| **Desktop controls** | Use keyboard shortcuts, select and copy text across messages, and stay linked in the tray with notifications. |
| **Themes** | Choose light, dark, system appearance, or custom colours. On Omarchy, follow your desktop theme. |
| **Privacy** | Hide locked chats behind a code, or the whole window behind an app lock. Nothing goes to a server of ours. |

## Install

| Platform | Installation |
|---|---|
| **macOS** | `brew install --cask crmne/tap/zapfast`, or [download the Mac app](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#macos). |
| **Arch Linux** | `yay -S zapfast-bin` |
| **Windows** | Choose your build on the [Download page](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#windows). |
| **Other Linux** | Find Nix, AppImage, and other options on the [Download page](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#linux). |
| **From source** | Follow [Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) for dependencies and commands. |

## Link your phone

1. Open ZapFast. It shows a QR code.
2. On your phone, open WhatsApp, then **Settings**, **Linked devices**,
   **Link a device**, and scan the code. Or click **Link with phone number**
   and enter the eight-character code on your phone.
3. Your recent chats arrive from the phone. Older messages follow as you
   scroll up.

The link survives restarts, and your phone does not need to stay online to
read what ZapFast has already stored. See
[Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) for the full
walkthrough and [How it links](https://zapfast.rocks/how-it-links/) for the
details.

## Guides and help

The complete guide lives at **[zapfast.rocks](https://zapfast.rocks/)**.

| Make your own theme | [Making a theme](https://zapfast.rocks/themes/) |

| Understand account risk | [Account safety](https://zapfast.rocks/what-is-zapfast/#account-safety) |
| Report a bug or propose a feature | Read [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), then use the [issue forms](https://github.com/crmne/zapfast/issues/new/choose). |

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening an issue or pull

```sh
cargo run --features demo -- --demo
```

[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) describes the architecture, [DEMO.md](DEMO.md) the
demo pages, screenshots, and recorded tours, and
[PACKAGING.md](PACKAGING.md) releases and packages.

Native notifications use Fastframe on Linux, macOS and Windows. ZapFast keeps
its account/chat routing, privacy settings, notification limits and sound
previews. Clicks open the announced message; reading a chat withdraws its
tracked notifications. OS permissions and notification presentation still apply.


## More native apps

**Want Spotify just as fast and native?** [Spotifast](https://spotifast.rocks)
is ZapFast's sibling. Both are built on
[fastframe](https://fastframe.dev).

ZapFast is an unofficial client and is not affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta.
Using an unofficial client may be against WhatsApp's terms of service and
could get an account suspended. Use it at your own risk. WhatsApp is a

Browser automation CLI for AI agents

Language: Rust

README

# agent-browser

Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

<p>
  <a href="https://vercel.com/labs#labs-products"><img alt="Vercel Labs Product" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/LABS-PRODUCT-0a0a0a.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=Vercel&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-browser"><img alt="npm version: agent-browser" src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/agent-browser.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/blob/main/LICENSE"><img alt="License: Apache-2.0" src="https://img.shields.io/github/license/vercel-labs/agent-browser.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-browser"><img alt="npm downloads per month: agent-browser" src="https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/agent-browser.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000&label=npm%20downloads" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser"><img alt="skills.sh" src="https://skills.sh/b/vercel-labs/agent-browser?style=for-the-badge" height="28"></a>
</p>

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install           # download Chrome for Testing (first time only)
```

- **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`.
- **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries.
- **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`.

Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation).

## Quick start

```bash
agent-browser open example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i       # interactive elements, each with a ref
agent-browser click @e1         # act on a ref from that snapshot
agent-browser get url           # check the result
agent-browser close
```

The snapshot for `example.com`:

```
- link "Learn more" [ref=e1]
```

- Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again.
- CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors).
- A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry.

The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start).

## How it works

The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured.

Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore).

## For AI agents

The CLI ships skills that match its version:

```bash
agent-browser skills get core                 # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows
agent-browser skills get core --ref commands  # one reference, such as the full command list
agent-browser skills get core --full          # adds the full command reference and templates
agent-browser skills list                     # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more
```

Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser):

```bash
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser
```

The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run
`agent-browser skills get core` and follow it.
```

For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server).

## Commands

Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser <command> --help` for one command.

| Group | Commands | Docs |
|---|---|---|
| Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) |
| Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) |
| Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) |
| Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) |
| Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) |
| Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) |
| Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) |
| Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) |
| Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) |
| Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) |
| Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) |

Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration).

## Platforms

Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host.

## Development

Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build:source               # builds the dashboard and the native CLI
pnpm link --global
agent-browser install
```

Run the Rust checks from `cli/`:

```bash
cargo fmt -- --check
cargo clippy
cargo test
cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1   # launches real headless Chrome
```

[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process.

## Documentation

- [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference
- [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration)
- [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries
- [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

## License

README

<div align="center">

# CalibRaw

**A free, open-source RAW photo editor for Linux, Android, Windows and macOS, with a complete photo-development workflow and AI tools that run locally.**

[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Duecki1/CalibRaw?label=Download&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/Duecki1/CalibRaw/releases/latest)
[![License: GPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue.svg)](COPYING)
[![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-Rust_1.92+-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)
[![Graphics: wgpu](https://img.shields.io/badge/Graphics-wgpu_%2F_WGSL-red.svg)](https://wgpu.rs/)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Linux_%7C_Android_%7C_Windows_%7C_macOS-green.svg)](https://github.com/Duecki1/CalibRaw/releases/latest)

[**Download**](#download) • [**Why CalibRaw**](#why-calibraw) • [**Features**](#key-features) • [**FAQ**](#faq) • [**Supported Formats**](#supported-formats) • [**Building**](#building-from-source)

[**Website**](https://calibraw.dueckis.de) • [**Discord**](https://discord.gg/yrY3JDJKsr) • [**Instagram**](https://www.instagram.com/calib.raw/)

</div>

<img width="100%" alt="CalibRaw desktop editor with light and color controls" src="docs/images/demos/develop-edit.png" />

<table>
  <tr>
    <td width="50%" align="center">
      <strong>Library</strong><br />
      <img width="100%" alt="Desktop library with folders, photo thumbnails and ratings" src="docs/images/demos/library.png" />
    </td>
    <td width="50%" align="center">
      <strong>AI Masks</strong><br />
      <img width="100%" alt="Animated demo of AI subject masking and separate subject and background adjustments" src="docs/images/demos/develop-masks-subject.gif" />
    </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td width="50%" align="center">
      <strong>Effects</strong><br />
      <img width="100%" alt="Animated demo of fog amount, density and scene depth controls" src="docs/images/demos/develop-effects-fog.gif" />
    </td>
    <td width="50%" align="center">
      <strong>Android</strong><br />
      <img width="100%" alt="Android library, color controls and AI subject mask" src="docs/images/demos/mobile-combined-transparent.png" />
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

Edit RAW files with sliders, curves, color grading and masks. AI tools can select a subject or the sky, remove objects and denoise high-ISO photos. Everything runs **on your device**, without an account or subscription.

---

## Download

| Platform | Get it |
| --- | --- |
| **Linux** (x86_64 / ARM64) | [Flathub](https://flathub.org/en/apps/io.github.Duecki1.CalibRaw), or `.AppImage` or `.deb` (Debian 13+, Ubuntu 24.04+) from the [latest release](https://github.com/Duecki1/CalibRaw/releases/latest) |
| **Android** (ARM64) | [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/de.duecki.calibraw/), or `.apk` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Duecki1/CalibRaw/releases/latest) |
| **Windows** (x86_64 / ARM64) | Installer or portable `.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Duecki1/CalibRaw/releases/latest) |
| **macOS** (Apple Silicon / Intel) | `.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Duecki1/CalibRaw/releases/latest) |

AI models are downloaded once, on first use and only after you agree; they are verified by SHA-256 and then run offline.

### Graphics requirements

CalibRaw processes photos on the GPU through Vulkan, Direct3D 12 or Metal. OpenGL is not supported: a GPU whose only driver is OpenGL cannot be used, and CalibRaw shows an "Unsupported graphics driver" notice instead of the editor.

| Platform | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| **Linux** | A Vulkan driver. GPUs without one (for example Intel Haswell, whose Mesa Vulkan driver `hasvk` is not conformant and hidden) can run on the CPU with Mesa's software driver lavapipe (`mesa-vulkan-drivers` or `vulkan-swrast`), which is slow. |
| **Android** | A Vulkan-capable GPU and driver. |
| **Windows** | Direct3D 12 or Vulkan. Without either, Windows' software renderer (WARP) is used. |
| **macOS** | Metal. |

Set `WGPU_BACKEND` (for example `vulkan`) to choose the graphics API yourself.

---

## Why CalibRaw

- **Photo-development controls:** Light, Tone Curve, Color, Color Mixer, Color Grading, Detail, Optics, Effects and Masks panels, with a scene-referred pipeline, Sigmoid tone mapping and highlight recovery.
- **Offline AI:** Subject, sky, depth and click-to-select object masks, AI Remove (Big-LaMa) that blends its fill into your photo's grain, and RawNIND denoise for Bayer and X-Trans RAWs.
- **Native interface and GPU processing:** Written in Rust with `wgpu`, WGSL compute shaders and an `egui` interface.
- **Android support:** The Android app uses the same engine and `.calibraw` sidecars as the desktop app, with layouts for touch controls.
- **Broad camera support:** Opens RAW files supported by LibRaw and Rawler, covering a wide range of camera makers and models; see the linked support lists below.
- **Fast library browsing:** Generates proxy-based previews and caches thumbnails and display metadata for quicker browsing.
- **Library organization:** Filter photos by rating and pick/reject flags, and sort by file modification date, filename, file size, rating or flag.
- **Effects with masks:** Apply depth-based fog, rain and relighting, wet surfaces with puddles and reflections, smoke, light rays, glow, halation, edge glow, neon and lens, motion, radial or tilt-shift blur to the whole photo or inside a mask.
- **Edit Replay:** Export a 30 FPS MP4 showing your edit step by step for Reels, Shorts or before/after posts.

---

## Key Features

- **Rust & GPU Compute:** Built with `egui` and `wgpu`, with compute shaders for image processing.
- **Color Grading & Point Color:** Sample colors directly with an eyedropper, fine-tune custom Hue, Saturation, and Luminance ranges, and preview affected areas with a live selection mask.
- **Demosaicing:** Shader-based Bayer RCD, Fujifilm X-Trans (Markesteijn 3-pass), and Dual Demosaicing to reduce noise and artifacts in high-ISO images.
- **Sigmoid Tone Mapping:** Smooth highlight roll-off inspired by modern scene-referred color workflows, paired with Opposed and LCh highlight recovery.
- **Local AI Tools (Offline):** Subject, sky, depth and object masks, AI Denoise, and AI Remove.
- **Android App:** An ARM64 NDK build with 16 KB memory page support, touch layouts, and MediaStore exporting.
- **Non-Destructive Edits:** All sliders, curves, and masks are saved to lightweight `.calibraw` JSON sidecar files.
- **Presets:** Save any combination of adjustment groups, masks and profile choices as a named preset, apply it in Develop or to a whole Library selection, and share it as a `.calibraw-preset` file. Imported `.xmp` presets stay as their source, so unsupported settings are kept for later versions; their tone curves, Point Color, lens corrections and Subject, Background, Sky, gradient and luminance-range masks are translated on load.
- **LUTs:** Import `.cube` 3D LUTs and apply one per photo with an Amount slider. Batch exports can apply a preset and a LUT to every photo without changing their edits.
- **Tiled Export & CLI:** Exports large RAW files in tiles to avoid GPU memory limits, plus a command-line tool for batch rendering.
- **JPEG XL Export:** Exports lossless `.jxl` images at 8-bit or 16-bit precision, including EXIF metadata when enabled.
- **Edit Replay:** Export a short 30 FPS MP4 that replays the current edit by category.

---

## Tooling & Workflow

### Color & Tone
- **Point Color:** Sample a color in global or mask HSL controls, refine its Hue/Saturation/Luminance span, preview the selected range, and apply targeted shifts.
- **8-Band Color Mixer:** Adjust Hue, Saturation, and Luminance across 8 individual color bands.
- **3-Way Color Grading:** Dedicated Shadows, Midtones, Highlights, and Global color wheels mapped through Oklab color space.
- **Tone Curves:** Luminance curve and individual Red, Green, and Blue splines with monotonic limits.
- **Sigmoid Tone Mapping:** Provides smooth, film-like highlight compression without harsh clipping.

### Demosaicing & Corrections
- **Bayer RCD:** Directional interpolation for standard Bayer sensors.
- **Fujifilm X-Trans:** Directional derivative and homogeneity demarcation pipeline for Fuji sensors.
- **Dual Demosaicing:** Blends edge-preserving and smoothed passes to suppress chroma noise at high ISOs.
- **Automatic Lens Correction:** Matches available camera and lens profiles through Lensfun and can automatically correct distortion, chromatic aberration and vignetting.
- **Chromatic Aberration Removal:** Works with any lens, profiled or not. Measures how far red and blue sit from green across the frame and moves them back into place, then removes the purple, blue and green fringes that remain along high-contrast edges.
- **HDR Merge:** Combine multiple bracketed RAW exposures into one extended-range image.
- **Focus Stacking:** Combine RAW frames focused at different distances into one image that is sharp throughout.

### Masking & AI
- **Masks:** Brush, Linear Gradient, Radial Gradient, and Shape masks with independent curves and adjustments.
- **AI Masks:** Subject and background (BiRefNet), sky (SkySeg U2Net), depth range (experimental; Distill-Any-Depth, with MoGe-2 normals and sky), click-to-select objects (SAM 2.1), and people with their face, skin, hair, clothes, lips, teeth or glasses on desktop (RF-DETR-Seg and Sapiens2, with BiRefNet outlines at High quality).
- **AI Remove:** Big-LaMa fills removed objects at native resolution where possible and restores the photo's own grain around the fill.
- **Clone & Heal:** Classic retouching brushes with aligned, fixed and registered source modes.
- **AI Denoise:** RawNIND denoises Bayer RAWs while demosaicing them and X-Trans RAWs in linear RGB.
- **Privacy:** Every model runs on your device. Models are downloaded only after you agree, and verified by SHA-256.

### Creative Effects

Apply effects to the whole photo or stack them on a local mask. The Effects card adds Glow, Halation, Grain and Vignette in one click; every effect is in the Add menu. Each card keeps its main controls visible, with optional details collapsed. Hide a card to compare, reset its settings, or remove it independently. While their card is open, Relight, Light Rays, Radial Blur, Tilt-Shift and Vignette also show controls on the photo: drag a light or center into place, and rotate or widen the Tilt-Shift focus band directly.

- **Blur & Movement:** Soften distractions with Blur, shape bokeh with Lens Blur, add directional trails with Motion Blur, zoom or spin with Radial Blur, or keep a band in focus with Tilt Shift. Feather the mask for a smooth transition.
- **Glow & Light Rays:** Glow spreads colored light from bright pixels selected by the mask; turn on Self-illuminating to let the mask itself emit light, which Scene light lets fall on the surroundings, Fog, Smoke, Rain and wet ground. Light Rays uses the mask to shape light shafts. Both can spread beyond the selection. Drag position pads to place a center or source; Precise position also lets you place a ray source beyond the image.
- **Relight:** Add a light that shapes the scene in depth. Drag the light on the photo (or use the same position pad as Light Rays) and scroll over it to move it in front of or behind the subject, and let nearer objects cast soft shadows. Surfaces facing the light brighten most; Ambient light dims the existing light for a stronger key light. Scene depth is generated automatically.
- **Edge Glow & Neon:** Trace image contours with colored outlines and halos. Both effects stay inside the mask; Neon's Original image control retains the photo behind the lines, and its Scene light lets the lines light their surroundings.
- **Fog & Smoke:** Add atmospheric haze or textured plumes. Fog's Scene depth control builds haze with distance; turn it off for an even-distance veil. Light glow makes both glow around Relight, Light Rays, Glow and Neon lights; Image lights adds the photo's own lamps, signs and lit windows in their colours.
- **Rain:** Add falling rain, its mist and the splashes it throws up on the ground. Streaks take their length from the photo's shutter speed and their softness from its lens, so they blur with whatever lies at their distance. Drops pass behind nearer objects using scene depth and take their light from their surroundings, so they show light against dark areas and dark against a bright sky. Streaks catch Relight, Light Rays, Glow, Neon and the photo's own lamps, and straightening the photo keeps them falling the same way.
- **Wet Surfaces:** Darken surfaces as water does and let the ground reflect the photo, with puddles that gather in the ground's low places, stop at kerbs, break up on its texture and blur with the lens. The ground is found in scene depth, so reflections meet what stands on it. Relight, Light Rays, Glow and Neon add highlights, and a Rain effect ripples the puddles.
- **Grain:** Add photographic texture with adjustable size, roughness, color, and seed. Use a local mask for selective grain or Fullscreen for a film finish.
- **Halation:** Add warm halos around bright highlights, with radius, highlight threshold, and warmth controls. The halo appears only inside the mask, including light from nearby highlights outside it.
- **Vignette:** Darken edges with negative amounts or brighten them with positive amounts. Adjust the falloff, shape, center, and highlight protection. Its center follows the cropped, rotated frame; the other position pads use the full image.
- **Pixelate:** Turn selected areas into a mosaic with adjustable block size.

---

## FAQ

**How is CalibRaw different from darktable or RapidRAW?**
All three are free. darktable offers detailed module-level control and a mature
color pipeline. RapidRAW's editing workflow inspired CalibRaw.
CalibRaw uses a native interface and GPU processing, with the same engine on desktop
and Android. It includes offline AI, creative effects such as depth-aware fog and
light rays, and Edit Replay videos.

**Does any of my data leave my device?**
No. Editing, AI masks, AI Remove and AI Denoise all run locally. CalibRaw only goes online to
download AI models or the ONNX Runtime, and only after you agree.

**Where does CalibRaw get the DCP profiles?**
On start, CalibRaw tries to automatically detect DCP files on your machine (windows, macOS only).

**Which cameras and files are supported?**
Anything LibRaw or Rawler supports, as well as JPEG, PNG, HEIC and TIFF; see [Supported Formats](#supported-formats).

---

## Supported Formats

### RAW

CalibRaw uses **LibRaw (master at 830ac96)** for broad camera compatibility, paired with **Rawler (0.8.0)** for DNG and JPEG-XL DNG streams. When LibRaw cannot open a camera RAW (for example a camera newer than its colour tables), CalibRaw retries it with Rawler. Together, they support RAW files from a wide range of camera models; check their maintained lists for specific compatibility.

Supported cameras: [LibRaw](https://www.libraw.org/supported-cameras) and [Rawler](https://github.com/dnglab/dnglab/blob/main/SUPPORTED_CAMERAS.md) (maintained by the dnglab project). Supported file extensions:

```text
.3fr   .ari   .arw   .bay   .bmq   .cap   .cine  .cr2   .cr3   .crw
.cs1   .dc2   .dcr   .dcs   .dng   .drf   .eip   .erf   .fff   .gpr
.iiq   .k25   .kc2   .kdc   .mdc   .mef   .mos   .mrw   .nef   .nefx
.nrw   .obm   .orf   .pef   .ptx   .pxn   .qtk   .raf   .raw   .rdc
.rw2   .rwl   .rwz   .sr2   .srf   .srw   .sti
```

### Rendered images

JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF and rendered TIFF files are edited with the same tools. They open looking exactly as captured, with embedded ICC profiles, Display P3, HLG/PQ HDR HEIF and EXIF orientation honored:

```text
.jpg   .jpeg  .jpe   .png   .heic  .heif  .hif   .tif   .tiff
```

When a camera saves RAW+JPEG (or RAW+HEIC), the Library shows each pair once, as the RAW. Turn this off under **Sort & filter → RAW + JPEG**.

---

## Architecture

CalibRaw is structured as a modular Rust workspace:

```text
CalibRaw/
├── crates/
│   ├── calibraw-core/  # Color transforms, decoders (LibRaw/Rawler), metadata, sidecars
│   ├── calibraw-gpu/   # wgpu pipelines, WGSL compute shaders, tiled renderer
│   ├── calibraw-ai/    # ONNX Runtime models (BiRefNet, SAM 2.1, LaMa, RawNIND)
│   ├── calibraw-ui/    # egui/eframe interface for desktop and touch
│   ├── calibraw-cli/   # Headless batch export CLI tool
│   └── calibraw-ffi/   # Android JNI and NativeActivity bridge
└── android/            # Android Gradle packaging
```

The reusable UI design library, [Moduwu Design](https://github.com/Duecki1/Moduwu),
is fetched automatically by Cargo from a pinned GitHub commit. See
[Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#design-library-setup) for design-library development.

### Headless CLI Export
Batch rendering can be run directly from the terminal:

```sh
calibraw-develop-export --input photo.ARW --output photo.jxl
```

---

## Building from Source

### Prerequisites
- **Rust Toolchain:** 1.92.0 or newer
- **System Dependencies:** `libclang`, `cmake`, `pkg-config`, and standard C/C++ build tools (for LibRaw and Lensfun)

### Desktop (Linux / Windows / macOS)

Cargo automatically downloads Moduwu Design from GitHub; no separate checkout
is required.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Duecki1/CalibRaw.git
cd CalibRaw
cargo run -p calibraw-ui --bin calibraw --release
```

For Linux sandbox builds, see the [local Flatpak workflow](docs/FLATPAK.md)
for setup, debugging, installation, validation, and unpublished release staging.

### Android (APK)
```sh
rustup target add aarch64-linux-android
cargo install cargo-ndk --version 4.1.2 --locked
./gradlew assembleDebug
```

---

## Acknowledgments

CalibRaw's shaders and tools draw on work from these projects:

- **[darktable](https://www.darktable.org/)**: Bayer RCD, X-Trans Markesteijn, Opposed highlight recovery, and Sigmoid tone mapping logic.
- **[GIMP](https://www.gimp.org/) & [Ansel](https://ansel.photos/)**: Laplace inpainting foundations and color normalization references.
- **[LibRaw](https://github.com/LibRaw/LibRaw), [Rawler](https://github.com/dnglab/dnglab), & [Lensfun](https://github.com/lensfun/lensfun)**: RAW decoding, DNG metadata extraction, and lens profile databases.
- **[RapidRAW](https://github.com/CyberTimon/RapidRAW)**: Interface and workflow layout inspiration.
- **[halation-dctl](https://github.com/hotgluebanjo/halation-dctl)**: Blur and frequency-separation approach behind the Halation effect.

*See [Third-Party Notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for complete licensing, attributions, and model sources.*

An agent runtime and tool protocol for principled agent concurrency

Language: Rust

README

# [Infinity](https://infinity.hydro.run)

Infinity is a Rust framework for building massively concurrent agentic systems, light enough to fit 75k agents in the memory of a Raspberry Pi. Infinity does for agents what async did for threads: instead of blocking on slow tools, Infinity agents run them concurrently, yield while they wait, and cost nothing until the next event arrives.

```rust
let system = AgentSystemBuilder::new_local(
    InMemoryConversationStore::new(),
    InMemoryStateStore::new(),
    StaticModel::new(provider, "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6").await?,
)
.start();

let mut thread = system.thread_builder().launch().await;
thread.send_user_text("Write a haiku about Rust").await?;

while let Some(event) = thread.recv().await {
    println!("{event:?}");
}
```

Between turns, an agent is pure data, just its conversation history with no task, no stack, and no open connection, so a waiting agent hibernates for free and wakes on the next message. The same agent code runs unchanged in a resident process on your laptop and on serverless platforms like AWS Lambda, where scale to zero is the default.

**Get started today at [infinity.hydro.run](https://infinity.hydro.run)!**

## Learn More

- **[Infinity Runtime](https://infinity.hydro.run/docs/infinity-runtime/overview)**: Build your first agent with the [quickstart](https://infinity.hydro.run/docs/infinity-runtime/quickstart/launching-your-first-agent), see how yielding turns and hibernation work in the [architecture guide](https://infinity.hydro.run/docs/infinity-runtime/architecture), and [deploy on AWS Lambda](https://infinity.hydro.run/docs/infinity-runtime/serverless/quickstart) with the included CDK constructs.

- **[Reactive Agent Protocol (RAP)](https://infinity.hydro.run/docs/rap/what-is-rap)**: Serve tools over the network without holding a connection open: results and subscription events are delivered whenever they are ready, even to agents that currently have no process at all. Existing MCP servers run unchanged through a compatibility layer, and anyone can implement the open [specification](https://infinity.hydro.run/docs/rap/spec/overview).

- **[Infinity Code](https://infinity.hydro.run/docs/infinity-code/overview)**: A coding agent built on the runtime for concurrent work: it runs builds and tests in the background while their output streams in, edits in parallel threads with stacked sandboxes, and hands you each result as a diff to review.

README

<p align="center">

</p>

<h1 align="center">Spotifast</h1>

<p align="center"><strong>Spotify, native and fast.</strong><br>A lightweight music app for Linux, macOS, and Windows.</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/download/"><strong>Download</strong></a> ·
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/">Getting started</a> ·
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/using-spotifast/">User guide</a> ·

</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="Cargo.toml"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Built_with-Rust-1ed760" alt="Built with Rust"></a>
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/download/"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux_%C2%B7_macOS_%C2%B7_Windows-24292f" alt="Linux, macOS, and Windows"></a>
  <a href="LICENSE"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-1ed760" alt="MIT license"></a>
</p>

Spotifast is a Spotify client written in Rust with
[egui](https://www.egui.rs) and [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the
framework behind a family of native desktop apps. It plays music through
[Spotify Soloist](https://spotifast.rocks/soloist/) or the built-in
[librespot](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot) player, and has no browser engine.

The interface includes complete
[translations for all supported languages](docs/_reference/translating.md#languages-and-coverage).

**Playback needs Spotify Premium.** Free accounts can browse and search, but
cannot play music through Spotifast.

![Spotifast Home with the playlist library, recommendations, queue, and player visible](docs/screenshot.png)

<details>
<summary><strong>Watch Spotifast in action</strong></summary>

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5f669ce-b3b7-4f8e-9933-976a78876c7e

</details>

[Features](#your-music-on-your-desktop) · [Install](#install) · [First playback](#start-listening) · [Mini player](#the-winamp-mini-player) · [MilkDrop](#music-in-motion) · [Help](#guides-and-help)

Since 0.15, setup leads with Spotify's
[Soloist player](https://spotifast.rocks/soloist/), with guided key setup,
one-time pairing and automatic renewal of expiring builds. New listeners and
people updating see this choice once after sign-in on supported platforms.
**Use the built-in player** keeps librespot, with Spotifast's EQ, visualizers,
local files and full queue editing. The choice is remembered.
On Linux with PipeWire, Soloist also supports Spotifast’s EQ and visualizers
through a private audio route. [Native audio support](https://spotifast.rocks/soloist/#native-audio)
adds EQ and visualizers on macOS 14.2 or newer, and visualizers on Windows 11,
including MilkDrop. Windows Soloist playback does not support audible EQ.
The Mac route keeps Soloist at full volume after redirecting its output,
then applies Spotifast’s volume after the visualizers, including mute. Phone
volume changes adjust that output level; Spotify’s indicator returns to 100%.
Windows visuals keep their level as Soloist’s volume falls and stop only when it is muted.
When enabled, Soloist appears as **This computer**; settings show the controls
that apply to it. Turning it off restores the built-in player's preferences.
While Soloist starts and its account is verified, the Spotify loading screen shows
**Verifying Soloist…** and waits to accept playback commands. Setup takes three
steps, and ends with choosing the named device in Spotify, with the built-in
player available as a quiet alternative below the card. If Soloist stops later,
a banner over the app says so while Spotifast restarts it, and offers **Try
again** if that does not work. **Settings → Spotify Soloist → Spotify access**
connects the separate Spotify session for Made for you, listening activity and
Spotify lyrics without changing players.

## Your music, on your desktop

| Feature | What you can do |
|---|---|
| **Library and search** | Browse playlists, Liked Songs, albums, artists, and podcasts. Discover upcoming albums on artist pages and open their countdown to pre-save. Search the catalogue and edit playlists you own. Copy a song's link, title, or artists from its menu. |
| **Local files** | Play the local files your playlists list from a folder you choose in Settings, at any sample rate. Names show spaces and accents correctly, including in cached playlists. |
| **Lyrics** | Spotify lyrics when the playback session is signed in, with LRCLIB as fallback. Temporary LRCLIB overloads retry and try search; older cached lyrics remain available during outages. |
| **Spotify Connect** | Play on this computer or control playback on your other devices, including Google Cast speakers and groups. Cast devices appear as they are discovered; frequently and recently chosen outputs rise to the top. Remote volume keeps your chosen level while Spotify updates. |
| **Queue** | Add songs to the queue, or choose **Play next** to put a song or selection first when playing on this computer. |
| **Themes** | Choose light, dark, system appearance, or custom colours, with one theme for light mode and one for dark mode that switch with the system. On Omarchy, follow your desktop theme. |
| **Desktop controls** | Use keyboard shortcuts and media keys. Keep music playing from the tray when supported by your desktop and settings, and start Spotifast with your computer, with its window or in the tray. |
| **Winamp mini player** | Use classic skins with an equalizer, playlist, and animated sound displays. |
| **MilkDrop** | Watch music-reactive visuals in a separate window or full screen. See platform availability below. |

## Install

| Platform | Installation |
|---|---|
| **macOS** | `brew install --cask crmne/tap/spotifast`, or [download the Mac app](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#macos). |
| **Arch Linux** | `yay -S spotifast-bin` |
| **Windows** | The installer or a portable ZIP, for x64 and ARM, from the [Download page](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#windows). |
| **Debian, Ubuntu** | The [DEB package](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#debian-and-ubuntu), then `sudo apt install ./spotifast_*.deb` |
| **Fedora** | The [RPM package](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#fedora), then `sudo dnf install ./spotifast-*.rpm` |
| **Other Linux** | Find Flatpak, AppImage, Nix, and other options on the [Download page](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#linux). |
| **From source** | Follow [Build from source](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/#build-from-source) for dependencies and commands. |

## Start listening

1. Register Spotifast with Spotify, as the sign-in screen shows: in the
   [Spotify developer dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard),
   click **Create app**, Spotify's name for this registration, with the
   redirect URI `http://127.0.0.1:8989/login` and **Web API** ticked. It takes
   about two minutes and gives you a Client ID. Spotify requires Premium on the
   account that registers, so a Free account can't do this step itself.
   [Getting started](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/#make-a-spotify-app)
   has the steps.
2. Paste the Client ID into Spotifast and choose **Sign in with Spotify**.
   Approve access in your browser, then return to the app to see your library.
3. To listen on this computer, open the device menu in the bottom player bar
   and choose **Set up playback here**, also available in Settings.
4. Complete the separate playback approval in your browser. Your computer
   appears as a Spotify Connect device named **Spotifast**.

Library access and local playback have separate approvals. Spotifast remembers
both using your computer's protected storage. See
[Getting started](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/) for the full walkthrough
and [How it connects](https://spotifast.rocks/how-it-connects/) for the details.

## The Winamp mini player

A classic look for your music, with Winamp 2 `.wsz` and Windows Media Player `.wmz` skins, an equalizer,
a playlist, and animated sound displays. Switch with **Ctrl+M**
(**Cmd+Shift+M** on macOS), the shrink button, or Settings.
The spectrum analyser and oscilloscope also work in the collapsed title bar.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/assets/images/winamp.png" alt="Spotifast's Winamp mini player with the built-in skin, equalizer, and playlist" width="320">
</p>

[Explore the mini player](https://spotifast.rocks/winamp/), including skins,
window sizes, controls, and the return to the main player.

## Music in motion

MilkDrop reacts to music playing on this computer, with more than 10,000
presets downloaded on first use. Open it from the visualiser button,
Settings, or the mini player's **V** menu.

![MilkDrop visualiser displaying coloured concentric patterns in Spotifast](docs/assets/images/milkdrop-poster.jpg)

Included on **Linux**, **macOS**, and **Windows Intel/AMD** builds.
It is not included in the Windows on ARM download.
[Read the MilkDrop guide](https://spotifast.rocks/milkdrop/) for presets,
controls, and fullscreen mode.

## Guides and help

The complete guide lives at **[spotifast.rocks](https://spotifast.rocks/)**.

| You want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| Sign in, set up playback, or configure themes, fonts, and proxies | [Getting started](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/) |
| Learn shortcuts, command-line controls, and updates | [Everyday use](https://spotifast.rocks/using-spotifast/) |
| Check storage sizes, clear cached audio and find stored files | [Settings and files](https://spotifast.rocks/settings-and-files/) |
| Understand scrolling performance and reduce loading delays | [Make it even faster](https://spotifast.rocks/make-it-even-faster/) |
| Fix "Spotify refused the audio key" or "Spotify is being slow" | [When something goes wrong](https://spotifast.rocks/troubleshooting/) |
| Understand what is stored and sent | [Privacy](https://spotifast.rocks/privacy/) · [How it connects](https://spotifast.rocks/how-it-connects/) |
| Check Spotify and librespot limitations | [What Spotify allows](https://spotifast.rocks/what-spotify-allows/) |
| Is it safe for my account? | [Account safety](https://spotifast.rocks/what-is-spotifast/#account-safety) |
| Report a bug or propose a feature | Read [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), then use the [issue forms](https://github.com/crmne/spotifast/issues/new/choose). |

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening an issue or pull
request. To look at the interface without a Spotify account, run:

```sh
cargo run --features demo -- --demo
```

Translations live in `assets/i18n/`; see
[Translating Spotifast](docs/_reference/translating.md). Release packaging
is described in [PACKAGING.md](PACKAGING.md).

## More native apps

**Want WhatsApp just as fast and native?** [ZapFast](https://zapfast.rocks)
is Spotifast's sibling. Both are built on
[fastframe](https://fastframe.dev).

## Spotify Connect updates

With local playback enabled, Spotify pushes changes from other devices over
Spotifast's existing Connect session. Playback changes trigger a refresh.
Volume-only changes appear directly for the active playback device without
an extra request; an unconfirmed volume change made in Spotifast takes
precedence. Push-triggered refreshes are at least a second apart and wait for
a pending playback read to finish. Changes received during that read are
folded into one follow-up.
Connect pushes are ignored when this computer is the active device both
before and after; position-only updates cause no requests. Regular polling
remains the fallback.

## Sonos playback

Sonos speakers use the Spotify Connect session for playback control. Enable
local playback first, then select the speaker in the device picker.

egui (pronounced "e-gooey") is a simple, fast, and highly portable immediate mode GUI library for Rust. egui runs on the web, natively, and [in your favorite game engine](#integrations).

egui aims to be the easiest-to-use Rust GUI library, and the simplest way to make a web app in Rust.

egui can be used anywhere you can draw textured triangles, which means you can easily integrate it into your game engine of choice.

[`eframe`](https://github.com/emilk/egui/tree/main/crates/eframe) is the official egui framework, which supports writing apps for Web, Linux, Mac, Windows, and Android.


## Example

``` rust
ui.heading("My egui Application");
ui.horizontal(|ui| {
    ui.label("Your name: ");
    ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut name);
});
ui.add(egui::Slider::new(&mut age, 0..=120).text("age"));
if ui.button("Increment").clicked() {
    age += 1;
}
ui.label(format!("Hello '{name}', age {age}"));
ui.image(egui::include_image!("ferris.png"));
```
